metadata.source: Digital Corpus of Sanskrit (DCS), text ID 215. http://www.sanskrit-linguistics.org/dcs/ Segmentation follows the DCS line/pāda boundaries; chapter and verse labels are taken from the DCS references.

children.text: tāṃ bhavānīṃ bhavānītakleśanāśaviśāradām
children.translated_text: Reverence to that <s>Bhavānī</s>, skilled in destroying the afflictions of worldly existence,

children.text: śāradāṃ śāradāmbhodasitasiṃhāsanāṃ namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to <s>Śāradā</s>, seated on a white lion-throne like an autumn cloud.

children.text: yuṣmākam ambaramaṇeḥ prathame mayūkhās te maṅgalaṃ vidadhatūdayarāgabhājaḥ
children.translated_text: May the first rays of the sun, lord of the sky, tinged with the redness of rising, bring you auspiciousness;

children.text: kurvanti ye divasajanmamahotsaveṣu sindūrapāṭalamukhīr iva dikpurandhrīḥ ||
children.translated_text: on the festivals of the birth of day they make the women of the quarters look as though their faces were red with vermilion.

children.text: baddhā yad arpaṇaraseṇa vimardapūrvam arthān kathaṃ jhaṭiti tān prakṛtān na dadyuḥ
children.translated_text: When words are bound by the relish of offering them, after being carefully rubbed and polished, how could they not at once yield those intended meanings?

children.text: caurā ivātimṛdavo mahatāṃ kavīnām arthāntarāṇy api haṭhād vitaranti śabdāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Like very gentle thieves, the words of great poets even forcibly bestow other meanings as well.

children.text: kāco maṇir maṇiḥ kāco yeṣāṃ te 'nye hi dehinaḥ
children.translated_text: Those for whom glass is a jewel and a jewel is glass are surely different embodied beings;

children.text: santi te sudhiyo yeṣāṃ kācaḥ kāco maṇir maṇiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the truly wise are those for whom glass is glass and a jewel is a jewel.

children.text: nanv āśrayasthitir iyaṃ tava kālakūṭa kenottarottaraviśiṣṭapadopadiṣṭā
children.translated_text: Indeed, O <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison, who instructed you in this manner of dwelling in ever more distinguished places?

children.text: prāg arṇavasya hṛdaye vṛṣalakṣmaṇo 'tha kaṇṭhe 'dhunā vasasi vāci punaḥ khalānām ||
children.translated_text: First you lived in the heart of the ocean, then in the throat of the bull-marked god, and now you dwell in the speech of wicked men.

children.text: draviṇam āpadi bhūṣaṇam utsave śaraṇam ātmabhaye niśi dīpakaḥ
children.translated_text: In misfortune it is wealth, at a festival an ornament, in fear for oneself a refuge, at night a lamp;

children.text: bahuvidhābhyupakārabharakṣamo bhavati ko 'pi bhavān iva sanmaṇiḥ ||
children.translated_text: some true jewel such as you is capable of bearing the weight of many kinds of service.

children.text: śrīr viśṛṅkhalakhalābhisārikā vartmabhir ghanatamomalīmasaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s>, like an unrestrained woman going to meet wicked lovers, moves along roads blackened with dense darkness,

children.text: śabdamātram api soḍhum akṣamā bhūṣaṇasya guṇinaḥ samutthitam ||
children.translated_text: unable to endure even the mere sound produced by the ornament of a virtuous man.

children.text: māne necchati vārayaty upaśame kṣmām ālikhantyāṃ hriyāṃ svātantrye parivṛtya tiṣṭhati karau vyādhūya dhairyaṃ gate
children.translated_text: When pride refuses, when shame is restrained and writes upon the ground, when independence turns away and stands aside, when courage has departed after tossing up its hands,

children.text: tṛṣṇe tvām anubadhnatā phalam iyatprāptaṃ janenāmunā yaḥ spṛṣṭo na padā sa eva caraṇau spraṣṭuṃ na saṃmanyate ||
children.translated_text: O craving, this much fruit has been obtained by this man who follows after you: the very one whom he did not touch with his foot is now not willing to touch his feet.

children.text: patatu vāriṇi yātu digantaraṃ viśatu vahnim atha vrajatu kṣitim
children.translated_text: Let it fall into water, go to another quarter, enter fire, or go to the earth:

children.text: ravir asāv iyatāsya guṇeṣu kā sakalalokacamatkṛtiṣu kṣatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: what loss is there, by so much, to this sun's qualities, which astonish the whole world?

children.text: sadvṛttayaḥ sadasadarthavivekino ye te paśya kīdṛśam amuṃ samudāharanti
children.translated_text: Look how people of good conduct, who discern good and bad meanings, explain this one:

children.text: caurāsatīprabhṛtayo bruvate yad asya tad gṛhyate yadi kṛtaṃ tad ahaskareṇa ||
children.translated_text: if what thieves, adulterous women, and the like say about him is accepted, then it was surely done by the maker of day.

children.text: pātaḥ pūṣṇo bhavati mahate nopatāpāya yasmāt kāle prāpte ka iha na yayur yānti yāsyanti vāstam
children.translated_text: The setting of the sun does not cause great distress, since, when the time has come, who here has not gone, does not go, or will not go to setting?

children.text: etāvat tu vyathayatitarāṃ lokabāhyais tamobhis tasminn eva prakṛtimahati vyomni labdho 'vakāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But this alone gives excessive pain: space has been obtained, in that very naturally vast sky, by darknesses that are outside the world.

children.text: paṅktau viśantu gaṇitāḥ pratilomavṛttyā pūrve bhaveyur iyatāpy athavā traperan
children.translated_text: Let them enter the row, counted in reverse order; by that much they might become earlier, or else feel ashamed.

children.text: santo 'py asanta iva cet pratibhānti bhānor bhāsāvṛte nabhasi śītamayūkhamukhyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, though real, they appear as though unreal in the sky covered by the sun's radiance, those headed by the moon, whose rays are cool, are like that.

children.text: gate tasmin bhānau tribhuvanasamunmeṣavirahavyathāṃ candro neṣyaty anucitam ato nāsty asadṛśam
children.translated_text: When that sun has gone, it is not improper, nor unlike its nature, that the moon should remove the pain caused by the lack of awakening of the three worlds.

children.text: idaṃ cetastāpaṃ janayatitarām atra yad amī pradīpāḥ saṃjātās timirahatibaddhodhuraśikhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But this produces even greater burning of the mind here: these lamps have arisen with smoky flames yoked to the destruction of darkness.

children.text: sūryād anyatra yaccandre 'py arthāsaṃsparśi tat kṛtam
children.translated_text: Whatever was done elsewhere than the sun, even in the moon, without touching the real matter,

children.text: khadyota iti kīṭasya nāma tuṣṭena kenacit ||
children.translated_text: that was the name 'firefly' given by someone pleased with an insect.

children.text: kīṭamaṇe dinam adhunā taraṇikarāntaritacārusitakiraṇam
children.translated_text: O jewel among insects, now by day your charming white rays are hidden by the sun's rays;

children.text: ghanasaṃtamasamalīmasadaśadiśi niśi yad virājasi tad anyat ||
children.translated_text: but if you shine at night, when the ten directions are stained by dense darkness, that is another matter.

children.text: sattvāntaḥsphuritāya vā kṛtaguṇādhyāropatucchāya vā tasmai kātaramohanāya mahaso leśāya mā svasti bhūt
children.translated_text: May there be no blessing for that tiny portion of light, whether it flickers inside living beings or is made worthless by the imputation of virtues, that frightens and deludes the timid.

children.text: yacchāyāchuraṇāruṇena khacatā khadyotanā khadyotanāmnāmunā kīṭenāhitayā hi jaṅgamamaṇibhrāntyā viḍambyāmahe ||
children.translated_text: For by this insect called a firefly, reddened by the touch of its own glow as it moves in the sky, we are mocked through the false notion that it is a moving jewel.

children.text: dantāntakuntamukhasaṃtatapātaghātasaṃtāḍitonnatagirir gaja eva vetti
children.translated_text: Only the elephant knows the pain of the repeated blows falling on its lofty head from the spear-points at the ends of teeth,

children.text: pañcāsyapāṇipavipañjarapātapīḍāṃ na kroṣṭukaḥ śvaśiśuhuṅkṛtinaṣṭaceṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: not the jackal, whose activity is ruined by the yelping of puppies, the pain caused by the fall of the thunderbolt-cage of the lion's paws.

children.text: atyunnativyasaninaḥ śiraso 'dhunaiṣa svasyaiva cātakaśiśuḥ praṇayaṃ vidhattām
children.translated_text: Let this young <s>cātaka</s> bird, addicted to excessive loftiness, now place its affection on its own head alone.

children.text: asyaitad icchati yadi pratatāsu dikṣu tāḥ svacchaśītamadhurāḥ kva nu nāma nāpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it wants this, where indeed, in the outspread quarters, are those clear, cool, sweet waters not to be found?

children.text: so 'pūrvaḥ rasanāviparyayavidhistat karṇayoś cāpalaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ sā madavismṛtasvaparadik kiṃ bhūyasoktena vā
children.translated_text: That unprecedented reversal of taste, that restlessness of the ears, that sight forgetful in intoxication of its own and others' quarters: why say more?

children.text: itthaṃ niścitavān asi bhramara he yad vāraṇo 'dyāpy asā antaḥśūnyakaro niṣeyata iti bhrātaḥ ka eṣa grahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O bee, brother, since you have decided in this way that this elephant is still to be avoided because its trunk is empty within, what is this obsession of yours?

children.text: tad vaidagdhyaṃ samucitapayastoyatattvaṃ vivektuṃ saṃlāpās te sa ca mṛdupadanyāsahṛdyo vilāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Let alone that cleverness of yours, fit to distinguish the true nature of milk and water, and that conversation, and that graceful movement charming with soft steps.

children.text: āstāṃ tāvad baka yadi tathā vetthi kiṃcicchlathāṃsas tūṣṇīm evāsitum api sakhe tvaṃ kathaṃ me na haṃsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O crane, friend, if you know anything in that way even with your shoulders drooping a little, how is it that you are not a swan to me even when you sit silently?

children.text: pathi nipatitāṃ śūnye dṛṣṭvā nirāvaraṇānāṃ navadadhighaṭīṃ garvonnaddhaḥ samuddhurakandharaḥ
children.translated_text: Having seen, fallen on an empty road, a fresh pot of curds with no cover, proud and with its neck held high,

children.text: nijasamucitās tās tāś ceṣṭā vikāraśatākulo yadi na kurute kākaḥ kāṇaḥ kadā nu kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: if the one-eyed crow, agitated by a hundred distortions, does not perform all those actions proper to itself, when indeed will it perform them?

children.text: nṛtyantaḥ śikhino manoharam amī śrāvyaṃ paṭhantaḥ śukā vīkṣyante na ta eva khalviha ruṣā vāryanta evāthavā
children.translated_text: Peacocks are seen dancing, and parrots reciting what is pleasing to hear; surely these are not angrily restrained here, are they?

children.text: pānthastrīgṛham iṣṭalābhakathanāllabdhānvayenāmunā sampratyetad anargalaṃ balibhujā māyāvinā bhujyate ||
children.translated_text: But now, through this deceitful eater of offerings, who has gained a connection by announcing a desired gain to a traveller's wife at her house, this is being consumed without restraint.

children.text: karabha rasabhāt kroṣṭuṃ vāñchasy aho śravaṇajvaraḥ śaraṇam athavānṛjvī dīrghā tavaiva śirodharā
children.translated_text: O camel, alas, you wish to cry out against the ass; what a fever of the ears! Or perhaps your own long, crooked neck is your refuge.

children.text: pṛthugalavilāvṛttiśrāntoccariṣyati vāk cirādiyati samaye ko jānīte bhaviṣyati kasya kim ||
children.translated_text: Your voice, wearied by the movement of your broad throat, will come out only after a long time; in so much time, who knows what will happen to whom?

children.text: antaśchidrāṇi bhūyāṃsi kaṇṭakā bahavo bahiḥ
children.translated_text: There are very many hollows inside, and many thorns outside;

children.text: kathaṃ kamalanālasya mā bhūvan bhaṅgurā guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: how could the qualities of the lotus-stalk not be fragile?

children.text: kiṃ dīrghadīrgheṣu guṇeṣu padma siteṣvavacchādanakāraṇaṃ te
children.translated_text: O white lotus, what is the reason for covering your long, very long fibres?

children.text: astyeva tān paśyati ced anāryā trasteva lakṣmīr na padaṃ vidhatte ||
children.translated_text: They certainly exist; but if an ignoble woman sees them, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, as though frightened, will not set foot there.

children.text: na paṅkād udbhūtir na jalasahavāsavyasanitā vapur digdhaṃ kāntyā sthalanalinaratnadyutimuṣā
children.translated_text: Your origin is not from mud, nor are you addicted to dwelling together with water; your body is smeared with a radiance that steals the brilliance of a jewel-like land-lotus.

children.text: vyadhāsyad durvedhā hṛdayalaghimānaṃ yadi na te tvam evaiko lakṣmyāḥ paramam abhaviṣyaḥ padam iha ||
children.translated_text: If the badly-disposing creator had not made lightness of heart in you, you alone would have become here the supreme seat of <s>Lakṣmī</s>.

children.text: uccair uccaratu ciraṃ cirī vartmani taruṃ samāruhya
children.translated_text: Let the cricket chirp loudly for a long time, after climbing a tree by the road;

children.text: digvyāpini śabdaguṇe śaṅkhaḥ sambhāvanābhūmiḥ ||
children.translated_text: when the quality of sound spreads through the quarters, the conch is the proper ground for esteem.

children.text: śaṅkho 'sthiśeṣaḥ sphuṭito mṛto vā procchvāsyate 'nyaśvasitena satyam
children.translated_text: It is true that a conch, reduced to bone, split open, dead as it is, is blown by another's breath;

children.text: kiṃ tūccaraty eva hi so 'sya śabdaḥ śrāvyo na yo yo na sadarthaśaṃsī ||
children.translated_text: yet it utters only that sound of its own which is audible and which proclaims no false meaning.

children.text: yathāpallavapuṣpās te yathāpuṣpaphalarddhayaḥ
children.translated_text: Where are those trees gone, mother, whose leaves were followed by flowers, whose flowers were followed by abundance of fruit,

children.text: yathāphalarddhisvārohā hā mātaḥ kvāgaman drumāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whose abundance of fruit was followed by their own rise in worth? Alas!

children.text: sādhv eva tavidhāv asya vedhā kliṣṭo na yad vṛthā
children.translated_text: It is quite proper in such a case that the creator was not troubled uselessly over this tree;

children.text: svarūpānanurūpeṇa candanasya phalena kim ||
children.translated_text: what use would fruit be to sandalwood, when it would not correspond to its own nature?

children.text: grathitaḥ eṣa mithaḥ kṛtaśṛṅkhalair viṣadharair adhiruhya mahājaḍaḥ
children.translated_text: This great inert sandalwood tree is encircled by poisonous serpents, bound together with interlinked chains, after they have climbed upon it;

children.text: malayajaḥ sumanobhir anāśrito yad ata eva phalena viyujyate ||
children.translated_text: because it is not resorted to by good blossoms, for that very reason it is deprived of fruit.

children.text: candane viṣadharān sahāmahe vastu sundaram aguptimatkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: We can endure poisonous serpents on sandalwood, since a beautiful thing has been left unguarded;

children.text: rakṣituṃ vada kim ātmagauravaṃ saṃcitāḥ khadira kaṇṭakās tvayā ||
children.translated_text: but tell me, O khadira tree, what self-respect were you trying to protect by amassing thorns?

children.text: yat kiṃcanānucitam apy ucitānuvṛtti kiṃ candanasya na kṛtaṃ kusumaṃ phalaṃ vā
children.translated_text: What impropriety, even if improper, has not been done by sandalwood in conformity with what is fitting: flower or fruit?

children.text: lajjāmahe vayam upakrama eva yāntas tasyāntikaṃ parigṛhītabṛhatkuṭhārāḥ ||
children.translated_text: We are ashamed to go near it even at the outset, carrying a great axe.

children.text: labdhaṃ cirād amṛtavat kim amṛtyave syād dīrghaṃ rasāyanavad āyur api pradadyāt
children.translated_text: If obtained after a long time, would it be like nectar, granting immortality? Would it bestow long life like an elixir?

children.text: etat phalaṃ yad ayam adhvagaśāpadagdhaḥ stabdhaḥ khalaḥ phalati varṣaśatena tālaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the fruit: scorched by travellers' curses, that rigid worthless palm bears fruit after a hundred years.

children.text: chinnas tṛptasuhṛt sa candanatarur yūyaṃ palāyyāgatā bhogābhyāsasukhāsikāḥ pratidinaṃ tā vismṛtās tatra vaḥ
children.translated_text: That sandalwood tree, whose friends had been satisfied, was cut down; you fled and came back, O serpents, and there you forgot those daily seats made pleasant by the habit of enjoyment.

children.text: daṃṣṭrākoṭiviṣolkayā pratikṛtaṃ tasya prahartur na cet kiṃ tenaiva saha svayaṃ na lavaśo yātāḥ stha bho bhoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If that assailant was not repaid with the flame of poison from the tips of your fangs, why did you yourselves not go to pieces together with that very tree, O serpents?

children.text: saṃtoṣaḥ kim aśaktatā kim athavā tasminn asaṃbhāvanā lobho vāyam utānavasthitir iyaṃ pradveṣa evāthavā
children.translated_text: Is it contentment, or incapacity? Or perhaps lack of expectation in that case? Is this greed, or is it instability, or rather sheer hatred?

children.text: āstāṃ khalv anurūpayā saphalayā puṣpaśriyā durvidhe sambandho 'nanurūpayāpi na kṛtaḥ kiṃ candanasya tvayā ||
children.translated_text: Let it be; O ill-disposed creator, why did you not make for sandalwood a connection with a fitting and fruitful beauty of flowers, even if an unfitting one was not made?

children.text: kiṃ jāto 'si catuṣpathe ghanatarachāyo 'si kiṃ chāyayā saṃnaddhaḥ phalito 'si kiṃ phalabharaiḥ pūrṇo 'si kiṃ saṃnataḥ
children.translated_text: What of it if you were born at a crossroads? What of your shade, though it is very dense? What of it if you stand equipped with fruit? What of your fruit-heavy fullness? What of it if you bend down?

children.text: he sadvṛkṣa sahasva samprati sakhe śākhāśikhākarṣaṇakṣobhāmoṭanabhañjanāni janataḥ svair eva duśceṣṭitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O good tree, friend, now endure the pulling of your branch-tips, the shaking, twisting, and breaking done by the people through their own misconduct.

children.text: sanmūlaḥ prathitonnatir ghanalasacchāyaḥ sthitaḥ satpathe sevyaḥ sadbhir itīdam ākalayatā tālo 'dhvagenāśritaḥ
children.translated_text: A palm tree with good roots, renowned height, and dense shining shade stood on a good road; thinking, 'It is to be served by good men,' a traveller took shelter under it.

children.text: puṃsaḥ śaktir iyaty asau tu phaled adyāthavā śvo 'thavā kāle kvāpy athavā kadācid athavā na tv eva vedhāḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: But a man's power goes only so far: that tree may bear fruit today, or tomorrow, or at some time, or someday, or not at all; the creator is not indeed under his control.

children.text: tvanmūle puruṣāyuṣaṃ gatam idaṃ dehena saṃśuṣyatā kṣodīyāṃsam api kṣaṇaṃ param ataḥ śaktiḥ kutaḥ prāṇitum
children.translated_text: At your root this human life has passed while the body dried up; after this, whence comes the strength to live even for the smallest moment?

children.text: tat svasty astu vivṛddhim ehi mahatīm adyāpi kā nas tvarā kalyāṇin phalitāsi tālaviṭapin putreṣu pautreṣu vā ||
children.translated_text: So may it be well with you; grow to great size. Even now, what haste have we? O auspicious palm tree, you may bear fruit for our sons or grandsons.

children.text: paśyāmaḥ kim ayaṃ prapatsyata iti svalpābhrasiddhakriyair darpād dūram upekṣitena balavat karmeritair mantribhiḥ
children.translated_text: A little cloud, whose action was easy to accomplish, was arrogantly disregarded from afar by ministers driven by powerful deeds, as they thought, 'Let us see what this one will attain.'

children.text: labdhātmaprasareṇa rakṣitum athāśakyena muktvāśāniṃ sphītas tādṛg aho ghanena ripuṇā dagdho girigrāmakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when that enemy cloud had gained room for itself, it became swollen and impossible to restrain; after casting down lightning, alas, it burned a village on the mountain.

children.text: sādhūtpātaghanaugha sādhu sudhiyā dhyeyaṃ dharāyām idaṃ ko 'nyaḥ kartum alaṃ tavaiva ghaṭate karmedṛśaṃ duṣkaram
children.translated_text: Well done, mass of cloud for raising calamities, well done! This should be pondered on earth by the wise: who else is able to do such a difficult deed? It befits you alone.

children.text: sarvasyaupayikāni yāni katicit kṣetrāṇi tatrāśaniḥ sarvān aupayikeṣu dagdhasikatāraṇyeṣv apāṃ vṛṣṭayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Lightning falls on the few fields that are useful to everyone; rains fall on all the useful burnt-sand deserts.

children.text: labdhāyāṃ tṛṣi gomṛgasya vihagasyānyasya vā kasyacid vṛṣṭyā syād bhavadīyayopakṛtir ity āstāṃ davīyasy adaḥ
children.translated_text: Let that distant thought remain, that by your rain there might be benefit when some cow, deer, bird, or other creature has become thirsty.

children.text: asyātyantam abhājanasya jaladāraṇyoṣarasyāpi kiṃ jātā paśya punaḥ punar eva paruṣā saivāsya dagdhā chaviḥ ||
children.translated_text: Look: for this utterly unfit, forest-barren salt ground too, what has been produced again and again except that same harsh, scorched appearance?

children.text: saṃtyajya pānācamanocitāni toyāntarāṇy asya siseviṣos tvām
children.translated_text: Abandoning other waters fit for drinking and sipping, when this man wishes to resort to you,

children.text: nirjaina jihreṣi jalair janasya jaghanyakāryaupayikaiḥ payodhe ||
children.translated_text: O ocean, do you not feel shame over waters useful only for the lowest tasks of people, O briny one?

children.text: āstrīśiśu prathita eṣa pipāsitebhyaḥ saṃrakṣyate 'mbudhir apeyatayaiva dūrāt
children.translated_text: Famous to women and children alike, this ocean is kept far away from the thirsty precisely because it is undrinkable.

children.text: daṃṣṭrākarālamakarālikarālitābhiḥ kiṃ bhāyayaty aparam ūrmiparamparābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why does it frighten others with rows of waves made terrible by lines of sea-monsters with dreadful tusks?

children.text: svamāhātmyaślāghāgurugahanagarjābhir abhitaḥ kruśitvā kliśnāsi śrutikuharam abdhe kim iti naḥ
children.translated_text: O ocean, why do you torment our ear-cavities by roaring all around with deep, weighty thunderings that praise your own greatness?

children.text: ihaikaś cūḍālo hy ajani kalaśād yasya sakalaiḥ pipāsor ambhobhiś culukam api no bhartum aśakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For here there was once born from a pot a single top-knotted sage; with all your waters he could not fill even a handful for himself when he was thirsty.

children.text: sarvāsāṃ trijagaty apām iyam asāv ādhāratā tāvakī prollāso 'yam athāmbudhe 'mbunilaye seyaṃ mahāsattvatā
children.translated_text: This being the support of all the waters in the three worlds is yours, O ocean; this surge is yours, O abode of waters; this is your great substantiality.

children.text: sevitvā bahubhaṅgabhīṣaṇatanuṃ tvām eva velācalagrāvasrotasi pānatāpakalaho yat kvāpi nirvāpyate ||
children.translated_text: Yet after men have resorted to you, whose body is terrifying with many breakers, the distress of thirst is somehow quenched by drinking from streams among the stones of the shore-mountain.

children.text: nodvegaṃ yadi yāsi yady avahitaḥ karṇaṃ dadāsi kṣaṇaṃ tvāṃ pṛcchāmi yad ambudhe kimapi tanniścitya dehyuttaram
children.translated_text: If you do not become agitated, and if for a moment you lend an attentive ear, I ask you something, O ocean; decide it and give me an answer.

children.text: nairāśyātiśayātimātranibhṛtair niḥśvasya yad dṛśyase tṛṣyadbhiḥ pathikaiḥ kiyat tadadhikaṃ syād aurvadāhād ataḥ ||
children.translated_text: When thirsty travellers are seen sighing, utterly restrained by an extreme excess of despair, how much greater can that be than the submarine fire that burns you?

children.text: bhidyate 'nupraviśyāntar yo yathārucyupādhinā
children.translated_text: It is split apart when something enters within, according to whatever limiting condition it happens to have.

children.text: viśuddhiḥ kīdṛśī tasya jaḍasya sphaṭikāśmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What sort of purity, then, belongs to that dull crystal stone?

children.text: cintāmaṇe bhuvi na kenacid īśvareṇa mūrdhnā dhṛto 'ham iti mā sma sakhe viṣīdaḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Cintāmaṇi</s>, my friend, do not grieve, saying, "I have not been borne on the head by any lord on earth."

children.text: nāsty eva hi tvadadhiropaṇapuṇyabījasaubhāgyayogyam iha kasyacid uttamāṅgam ||
children.translated_text: For here there is no one whose highest limb is fit for the good fortune, rooted in merit, of having you set upon it.

children.text: saṃvittir asty atha guṇāḥ pratibhānti loke taddhi praśastam iha kasya kim ucyatāṃ vā
children.translated_text: There is consciousness, and virtues shine forth in the world; that indeed is praiseworthy here. Of whom, then, and what, is one to speak?

children.text: nanv evam eva sumaṇe luṭa yāvadāyus tvaṃ me jagatprasahane 'tra kathāśarīram ||
children.translated_text: Still, O good jewel, roll about just so as long as life lasts; here you are the very body of my tale about the overpowering of the world.

children.text: cintāmaṇes tṛṇamaṇeś ca kṛtaṃ vidhātrā kenobhayor api maṇitvam adaḥ samānam
children.translated_text: By the creator, what has been done to the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> and to the grass-jewel, that this jewelhood is the same for both?

children.text: naiko 'rthitāni dadann arthijanāya khinno gṛhṇañ jarattṛṇalavaṃ tu na lajjate 'nyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One is not wearied while giving requested objects to petitioners, while the other is not ashamed as it receives a bit of old grass.

children.text: dūre kasyacid eṣa ko 'py akṛtadhīr naivāsya vetty antaraṃ mānī ko 'pi na yācate mṛgayate ko 'py alpam alpāśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Some undiscerning man is far away and does not know its difference; some proud man does not beg; some petty-minded man seeks only a little.

children.text: itthaṃ prārthitadānadurvyasanino naudāryarekhojjvalā jātānaipuṇadustareṣu nikaṣasthāneṣu cintāmaṇeḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, for the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s>, addicted to the vice of granting what is asked, no bright line of generosity has appeared in testing-places difficult because of acquired skill.

children.text: parārthe yaḥ pīḍām anubhavati bhaṅge 'pi madhuro yadīyaḥ sarveṣām iha khalu vikāro 'py abhimataḥ
children.translated_text: When a thing suffers crushing for another's sake, is sweet even when broken, and whose alteration is indeed pleasing to everyone here,

children.text: na samprāpto vṛddhiṃ sa yadi bhṛśam akṣetrapatitaḥ kim ikṣor doṣo 'yaṃ na punar aguṇāyā marubhuvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if it has not attained growth because it fell in utterly unsuitable ground, how is this the fault of the sugarcane, and not rather of the meritless desert-land?

children.text: āmrāḥ kiṃ phalabhāranamraśiraso ramyā kim ūṣmacchidaḥ sacchāyāḥ kadalīdrumāḥ surabhayaḥ kiṃ puṣpitāś campakāḥ
children.translated_text: Are there mango trees with heads bent under the weight of fruit? Are there lovely plantain trees, cutting off the heat with good shade? Are there fragrant campakas in bloom?

children.text: etās tā niravagrahograkarabhollīḍhārdharūḍhāḥ punaḥ śamyo bhrāmyasi mūḍha nirmaruti kiṃ mithyaiva martuṃ marau ||
children.translated_text: Those are the śamī trees, half-grown and repeatedly licked by fierce, unrestrained camels. O fool, why do you wander in the windless desert only to die in vain?

children.text: ājanmanaḥ kuśalam aṇv api re kujanman pāṃso tvayā yadi kṛtaṃ vada tat tvam eva
children.translated_text: O low-born dust, tell me yourself whether even the smallest good has been done by you from birth.

children.text: utthāpito 'sy analasārathinā yadarthaṃ duṣṭena tat kuru kalaṅkaya viśvam etat ||
children.translated_text: The wicked wind, whose charioteer is fire, has raised you up for a certain purpose; do that very thing: stain this whole world.

children.text: niḥsārāḥ sutarāṃ laghuprakṛtayo yogyā na kārye kvacicchuṣyanto 'dya jarattṛṇādyavayavāḥ prāptāḥ svatantreṇa ye
children.translated_text: Those who are utterly without substance, very light by nature, fit for no task at all, drying up today as parts of old straw and the like, have come by one who is independent.

children.text: antaḥsāramukhena dhig aho te mārutenāmunā paśyātyantacalena sadma mahatām ākāśam āropitā ||
children.translated_text: Shame on them, alas: under the guise of having inner substance, by this extremely unstable wind they have been lifted up to the sky, the dwelling of the great. See!

children.text: ye jātyā laghavaḥ sadaiva gaṇanāṃ yātā na ye kutracit padbhyām eva vimarditāḥ pratidinaṃ bhūmau nilīnāś ciram
children.translated_text: Those who are light by birth, who have never been counted anywhere, who were trampled every day by feet and long lay hidden on the ground,

children.text: utkṣiptāś capalāśayena marutā paśyāntarikṣe 'dhunā tuṅgānām uparisthitiṃ kṣitibhṛttāṃ kurvanty amī pāṃsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: now, lifted up by a wind of fickle intention, look: these dust particles stand above the lofty ones and play the part of mountains in the sky.

children.text: re dandaśūka yad ayogyam apīśvaras tvāṃ vātsalyatau nayati nūpuradhāma satyam
children.translated_text: O snake, it is true that the lord, out of affection, brings you, though unworthy, to the place of an anklet.

children.text: āvarjitālikulaṃkṛtir mūrchitāni kiṃ śiñjitāni bhavataḥ kṣayam eva kartum ||
children.translated_text: But are your jinglings, with their form imitating a bent swarm of bees and faintly sounding, meant only to bring about your destruction?

children.text: maulau sanmaṇayo gṛhaṃ giriguhā tyāgitvam ātmatvaco niryatnopanataś caiva vṛttir anilair ekatra caryedṛśī
children.translated_text: On one side, good jewels on the head, a home in a mountain cave, renunciation of one's own skin, effortless livelihood supplied by winds: such is this way of life.

children.text: anyatrānṛju vartma vāg dvirasanā dṛṣṭau viṣaṃ dṛśyate yā dhik tām anu dīpako jvalati bho bhogin sakhe kiṃ nv idam ||
children.translated_text: On the other side, a crooked path, a forked tongue, and poison visible in the glance. Shame on that, O serpent, my friend! Why does a lamp burn after you?

children.text: kallolavellitadṛṣatparuṣaprahārai ratnāny amūni makarālaya māvamaṃsthāḥ
children.translated_text: O abode of sea-monsters, do not despise those jewels because of the rough blows of stones tossed by rolling waves.

children.text: kiṃ kaustubhena vihito bhavato na nāma yācñāprasāritakaraḥ puruṣottamo 'pi ||
children.translated_text: Was not even <s>Puruṣottama</s>, his hand stretched out in supplication, made famous by you through the <s>Kaustubha</s>?

children.text: bhūyāṃsy asya mukhāni nāma viditaivāste mahāprāṇatā kadravāḥ satprasavo 'yam atra kupite cintyaṃ yathedaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: Many indeed are his mouths; his mighty breath is well known; he is this noble offspring of <s>Kadrū</s>; when he is angry, this world must be considered accordingly.

children.text: trailokyādbhutam īdṛśaṃ tu caritaṃ śeṣasya yenāpi sā pronmṛjyeva nivartitā viṣadharajñāteyadurvṛttitā ||
children.translated_text: But this conduct of <s>Śeṣa</s> is such a wonder in the three worlds: by it he has, as it were, wiped away and turned back the misconduct of his poisonous kin.

children.text: varṣe samasta ekaikaḥ ślāghyaḥ ko 'py eṣa vāsaraḥ
children.translated_text: In the whole year, each single day is somehow praiseworthy,

children.text: janair mahattayā nīto yo na pūrvair na cāparaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when it has been brought to greatness by people, whether not by those before or not by those after.

children.text: ābaddhakṛtrimasaṭājaṭilāṃsabhittir āropito mṛgapateḥ padavīṃ yadi śvā
children.translated_text: If a dog, its shoulder-wall matted with an artificial mane tied on, has been placed in the rank of the lord of beasts,

children.text: mattebhakumbhataṭapāṭanalampaṭasya nādaṃ kariṣyati kathaṃ hariṇādhipasya ||
children.translated_text: How will it make the roar of the lord of deer, who is eager to split open the temples of rutting elephants?

children.text: kim idam ucitaṃ śuddheḥ śliṣṭaṃ svapakṣasamunnateḥ phalapariṇater yuktaṃ prāptaṃ guṇapraṇayasya vā
children.translated_text: What is this? Is it fitting for purity, coherent with the rise of one's own side, proper for the maturing of fruit, or attained through affection for merit?

children.text: kṣaṇam upagataḥ karṇopāntaṃ parasya puraḥ sthitān viśikha nipatan krūraṃ dūrān nṛśaṃsa nihaṃsi yat ||
children.translated_text: O arrow, in that you strike down cruelly from afar those who have for a moment come near another's ear and stand before him, you are merciless.

children.text: amī ye dṛśyante nanu subhagarūpāḥ saphalatā bhavaty eṣāṃ yasya kṣaṇam upagatānāṃ viṣayatām
children.translated_text: These that are seen here are surely handsome in form, and fruitfulness belongs to those who for a moment come within his range.

children.text: nirāloke loke katham idam aho cakṣur adhunā samaṃ jātaṃ sarvair na samam athavānyair avayavaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Alas, in a world without light, how has this eye now become equal to all? Or rather, it has not become equal to the other limbs.

children.text: āhūteṣu vihaṅgameṣu maśako nāyān puro vāryate madhevāridhi vā vasaṃstṛṇamaṇir dhatte maṇīnāṃ rucam
children.translated_text: When the birds have been summoned, a mosquito does not come forward or is not kept back; or, dwelling in a sea of liquor, a grass-jewel assumes the luster of jewels.

children.text: khadyoto 'pi na kampate pracalituṃ madhye 'pi tejasvināṃ dhik sāmānyam acetanaṃ prabhum ivānāmṛṣṭatattvāntaram ||
children.translated_text: Even a firefly does not tremble to move in the midst of the brilliant. Shame on the common, senseless thing, like a lord whose inner reality has not been examined.

children.text: hemakāra sudhiye namo 'stu te dustareṣu bahuśaḥ parīkṣitum
children.translated_text: O goldsmith, homage to your good judgment, since you test many times amid difficult matters,

children.text: kāñcanābharaṇam aśmanā samaṃ yat tvayaivam adhiropyate tulām ||
children.translated_text: in that a golden ornament and a stone are thus placed by you alone upon the balance together.

children.text: vṛtta eva sa ghaṭo 'ndhakūpa yas tvatprasādam api netum akṣamaḥ
children.translated_text: O blind well, that pot alone is truly rounded which is unable even to carry away your favor,

children.text: mudritaṃ tv adhamaceṣṭitaṃ tvayā tanmukhāmbukaṇikāḥ pratīcchatā ||
children.translated_text: but your low behavior has been sealed by you, as you receive the drops of water from its mouth.

children.text: tṛṇamaṇer manujasya ca tattvataḥ kim ubhayor vipulāśayatocyate
children.translated_text: Of the grass-jewel and a man, in truth, how can breadth of heart be spoken of in both alike,

children.text: tanutṛṇāgralavāvayavair yayor avasite grahaṇapratipādane ||
children.translated_text: when the proof and explanation of the grasping of both is concluded by tiny fragments of the tips of thin grass?

children.text: śatapadī sati pādaśate kṣamā yadi na goṣpadam apy ativartitum
children.translated_text: If a centipede, though it has a hundred feet, is unable to step over even a cow's hoofprint,

children.text: kim iyatā dvipadasya hanumato jalanidhikramaṇe vivadāmahe ||
children.translated_text: why should we dispute so much about the two-footed <s>Hanumat</s> crossing the ocean?

children.text: na guruvaṃśaparigrahaśauṇḍatā na ca mahāguṇasaṃgrahaṇādaraḥ
children.translated_text: There is no confident attachment to a venerable lineage, nor any concern for collecting great virtues,

children.text: phalavidhānakathāpi na mārgaṇe kim iha lubdhakabālagṛhe 'dhunā ||
children.translated_text: nor even talk of producing fruit in the matter of an arrow; what is there now in the young hunter's house?

children.text: tanutṛṇāgradhṛtena hṛtaś ciraṃ ka iva tena na mauktikaśaṅkayā
children.translated_text: Who has not long been deceived by that water-drop held on the tip of a thin blade of grass, through the suspicion that it was a pearl?

children.text: sa jalabindur aho viparītadṛg jagad idaṃ vayam atra sacetanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Alas, that water-drop sees perversely: 'This whole world is insentient, and we alone here are conscious.'

children.text: budhyāmahe na bahudhāpi vikalpayantaḥ kair nāmabhir vyapadiśema mahāmatīṃstān
children.translated_text: Even after considering in many ways, we do not understand by what names we should designate those great-minded ones

children.text: yeṣām aśeṣabhuvanābharaṇasya hemnas tattvaṃ vivektum upalāḥ paramaṃ pramāṇam ||
children.translated_text: for whom stones are the supreme authority for discerning the true nature of gold, the ornament of the whole world.

children.text: saṃrakṣituṃ kṛṣim akāri kṛṣīvalena paśyātmanaḥ pratikṛtis tṛṇapūruṣo 'yam
children.translated_text: To protect the crop, the farmer made this straw man; look, it is a likeness of himself.

children.text: stabdhasya niṣkriyatayāstabhiyo 'sya nūnam aśnanti gomṛgagaṇāḥ pura eva sasyam ||
children.translated_text: Surely, because this stiff one is inactive, the fearless herds of cattle and deer eat the grain right in front of him.

children.text: kasyānimeṣanayane vidite divaukolokād ṛte jagati te api vai gṛhītvā
children.translated_text: Apart from the world of the sky-dwellers, where are your unwinking eyes known in this world? Even having taken those too,

children.text: piṇḍaprasāritamukhena time kim etad dṛṣṭaṃ na bāliśa viśad baḍiśaṃ tvayāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O fish, with your mouth stretched out for a lump, did you not see, foolish one, the clear hook inside?

children.text: puṃstvād api pravicaled yadi yady adho 'pi yāyād yadi praṇayane na mahān api syāt
children.translated_text: Even if one should fall away from manhood, even if one should go downward, even if one were not great in attracting favor,

children.text: abhyuddharet tad api viśvam itīdṛśīyaṃ kenāpi dik prakaṭitā puruṣottamena ||
children.translated_text: still he would raise up the universe: such a direction was revealed by some <s>Puruṣottama</s>.

children.text: svālpāśayaḥ svakulaśilpavikalpam eva yaḥ kalpayan skhalati kācavaṇik piśācaḥ
children.translated_text: That petty-minded glass-merchant, a fiend, who imagines only the variations of his own family craft and stumbles,

children.text: grastaḥ sa kaustubhamaṇīndrasapatnaratnaniryatnagumphanakavaikaṭikerṣyayāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is inwardly consumed by envy of a maker of settings who effortlessly strings jewels rivaling the lordly <s>Kaustubha</s> gem.

children.text: tatpratyarthitayā vṛto na tu kṛtaḥ samyak svatantro bhayāt svasthas tān na nipātayed iti yathākāmaṃ na saṃpoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: It was chosen as his adversary, but not made properly independent out of fear; it was not nourished as it pleased, lest, being healthy, it should strike them down.

children.text: saṃśuṣyan pṛṣadaṃśa eṣa kurutāṃ mūkaḥ sthito 'py atra kiṃ gehe kiṃ bahunā 'dhunā gṛhapateś caurāś caranty ākhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This gadfly, drying up and remaining mute even while present here, may do what? In short, now in the house the householder's mice move about like thieves.

children.text: evaṃ cet sarasasvabhāvamahimā jāḍyaṃ kim etādṛśaṃ yady eṣā ca nisargataḥ sarasatā kiṃ granthimattedṛśī
children.translated_text: If the greatness of its nature is so full of sap, why such dullness? And if this juiciness is natural, why such knotty thickness?

children.text: mūlaṃ cecchucipaṅkajaśrutir iyaṃ kasmād guṇā yady amī kiṃ chidrāṇi mṛṇāla bhavatas tattvaṃ na manyāmahe ||
children.translated_text: If this root is pure and lotus-like in repute, why this? If these are virtues, why are they holes? O lotus-fiber, we do not understand your reality.

children.text: ye digdhveva kṛtā viṣeṇa kusṛtir yeṣāṃ kiyad bhaṇyate lokaṃ hantum anāgasaṃ dvirasanā randhreṣu ye jāgrati
children.translated_text: Those who are as if smeared with poison, whose crooked course is made, of whom how much can be said, who with two tongues keep watch in holes to kill the innocent world:

children.text: vyālās te 'pi dadhaty amī sadasator mūḍhā maṇīn mūrdhabhir naucityād guṇaśalināṃ kvacid api bhraṃśo 'styalaṃ cintayā ||
children.translated_text: even those snakes, foolish as they are, bear jewels on their heads, for the distinction between worthy and unworthy. There is no fall anywhere for the virtuous; enough of anxiety.

children.text: aho strīṇāṃ krauryaṃ hatarajani dhik tvām atiśaṭhe vṛthāprakrānteyaṃ timirakabarīviślathadhṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, the cruelty of women! O ruined night, shame on you, most deceitful one; this loosened holding of your braid of darkness has been undertaken in vain.

children.text: avaktavye pāte jananayananāthasya śaśinaḥ kṛtaṃ snehasyāntocitam udadhimukhyair nanu jaḍaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the unspeakable fall of the moon, lord of people's eyes, the end proper to affection has indeed been made by dull things, chiefly the ocean.

children.text: aho gehenardī divasavijigīṣājvararujā pradīpo 'yaṃ sthāne glapayati mṛṣāmūn avayavān
children.translated_text: Ah, in the house, afflicted by the fever-pain of wishing to conquer the day, this lamp, in its place, falsely wastes away these limbs.

children.text: udāttasvacchandākramaṇahṛtaviśvasya tamasaḥ parispandaṃ draṣṭuṃ mukham api ca kiṃ soḍham amunā ||
children.translated_text: Could it even endure the movement of the face of darkness, whose free and lofty advance had seized the universe?

children.text: nāmāpy anyataror nimīlitam abhūt tat tāvad unmīlitaṃ prasthāne skhalataḥ svavartmani vidher apy udgṛhītaḥ karaḥ
children.translated_text: Even the name of one of the two had been closed; that at least has been opened. The hand of fate too, stumbling on its own path at departure, has been grasped.

children.text: lokaś cāyam aniṣṭadarśanakṛtād dṛgvaiśasān mocito yuktaṃ kāṣṭhika lūnavān yad asi tām āmrālim ākālikīm ||
children.translated_text: And this world has been freed from the distress of sight caused by seeing what is undesirable. It is fitting, O woodcutter, that you have cut down that mango row out of season.

children.text: vātāhāratayā jagadviṣadharair āśvāsya niḥśeṣitaṃ te grastāḥ punar abhratoyakaṇikātīvravratair barhibhiḥ
children.translated_text: By living on wind, the poison-bearing serpents of the world had been reassured and then finished off by peacocks, whose fierce vow was sustained by tiny drops of cloud-water;

children.text: te 'pi krūracamūrucarmavasanair nītāḥ kṣayaṃ lubdhakair dambhasya sphuritaṃ vidann api jano jālmo guṇanīhate ||
children.translated_text: and those peacocks in turn were destroyed by hunters wearing cruel antelope-skins. Though people know the flashing display of hypocrisy, they are foolish, struck down by supposed virtue.

children.text: ūḍhā yena mahādhuraḥ suviṣame mārge sadaikākinā soḍho yena kadācid eva na nije goṣṭhe 'nyaśauṇḍadhvaniḥ
children.translated_text: He who bore the great burden on an exceedingly difficult road, always alone, and who never once endured in his own herd the bellowing of another drunken bull,

children.text: āsīd yas tu gavāṃ gaṇasya tilakas tasyaiva sampraty aho dhik kaṣṭaṃ dhavalasya jātajaraso goḥ paṇyam udghoṣyate ||
children.translated_text: he who was the very ornament of the whole herd of cattle: alas, now, shame and misery, that same white bull, grown old, is cried out for sale.

children.text: asthānodyogaduḥkhaṃ jahihi na hi nabhaḥ paṅgusaṃcārayogyaṃ svāyāsāyaiva sādho tava śalabha javābhyāsadurvāsaneyam
children.translated_text: Abandon the misery of effort in an unsuitable place; the sky is not fit for the movement of a lame man. O good grasshopper, this bad habit of practicing speed is only for your own exhaustion.

children.text: te devasyāpy acintyāś caṭulitabhuvanābhogahelāvahelāmūlotkhātānumārgāgatagiriguravas tārkṣyapakṣāgravātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those winds from the tips of <s>Tārkṣya</s>'s wings are inconceivable even to the god: in sport they uproot the very roots of mountains, heavy because they have come along a path, with contempt for the agitation of the expanse of the worlds.

children.text: candreṇaiva taraṅgabhaṅgimukharaṃ saṃvardhyamānāmbhaso dadyur jīvitam eva kiṃ girisaritsrotāṃsi yady ambudheḥ
children.translated_text: If mountain-river streams, whose waters are increased by the moon alone and made noisy by broken waves, could actually give life to the ocean,

children.text: teṣv eva pratisaṃvidhānavikalaṃ paśyatsu sākṣiṣv iva drāg darpoddhuram āgateṣv api na sa kṣīyeta yady anyathā ||
children.translated_text: then, even when those very streams had come at once swollen with pride, while their helpless witnesses looked on as if unable to make any response, that ocean would not diminish. But it is otherwise.

children.text: kilaikaculukena yo munir apāram abdhiṃ papau sahasram api ghasmaro 'vikṛtam eṣa teṣāṃ pibet
children.translated_text: The sage who drank the boundless ocean with a single handful: this devourer could drink even a thousand of those without alteration.

children.text: na sambhavati kiṃ tv idaṃ bata vikāsidhāmnā vinā sad apy asad iva sthitaṃ sphuritam anta ojasvinām ||
children.translated_text: Yet this cannot happen without expansive brilliance. Even when present, the shining power within the mighty remains as if absent.

children.text: grāvāṇo 'tra vibhūṣaṇaṃ trijagato maryādayā sthīyate nanv atraiva vidhuḥ sthito hi vibudhāḥ sambhūya pūrṇāśiṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Here stones are an ornament; the moon, ornament of the three worlds, remains here within its proper bounds; here, indeed, the gods gathered with complete blessings;

children.text: śete codgatanābhipadmavilasadbrahmeha devaḥ svayaṃ daivād eti jaḍaḥ svakukṣibhṛtaye so 'pyambudhir nimnatām ||
children.translated_text: and here the god himself lies, with <s>Brahmā</s> shining on the lotus that has risen from his navel. Yet by fate even that dull ocean sinks down, merely to fill its own belly.

children.text: anīrṣyā śrotāro mama vacasi ced vacmi tad ahaṃ svapakṣād bhetavyaṃ na tu bahu vipakṣāt prabhavataḥ
children.translated_text: If my hearers are free from envy toward my words, then I will say this: one should fear one's own side, not the much stronger opposing side.

children.text: tamasy ākrāntāśe kiyad api hi tejo 'vayavinaḥ svaśaktyā bhānty ete divasakṛti satyeva na punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When darkness has occupied the quarters, these small portions of light shine by their own power only when the sun truly exists, and not otherwise.

children.text: etat tasya mukhāt kiyat kamalinīpatre kaṇaṃ vāriṇo yan muktāmaṇir ity amaṃsta sa jaḍaḥ śṛṇvan yad asmād api
children.translated_text: How much was that from his mouth? The dull fellow thought a drop of water on a lotus leaf was a pearl, though he heard so from this one too.

children.text: aṅgulyagralaghukriyāpravilayinyādīyamāne śanaiḥ kutroḍḍīyagato mamety anudinaṃ nidrāti nāntaḥśucā ||
children.translated_text: As it is slowly taken away, disappearing through the slight motion of a fingertip, he sleeps day after day with inner grief, thinking, 'Where has mine flown off to?'

children.text: āste 'traiva sarasy aho bata kiyān saṃtoṣapakṣagraho haṃsasyāsya manāṅ na dhāvati manaḥ śrīdhāmni padme kvacit
children.translated_text: He stays right here in the lake. Ah, how great is this swan's attachment to contentment: his mind does not run even a little toward the lotus, the abode of beauty.

children.text: supto 'dyāpi na budhyate tad itarāṃs tāvat pratīkṣāmahe velām ity udaraṃpriyā madhulihaḥ soḍhuṃ kṣaṇaṃ na kṣamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'It is still sleeping today; it has not awakened. So long we shall wait for the others, for the right moment.' But the honey-drinkers, fond of their bellies, cannot endure even an instant.

children.text: bhekena kvaṇatā saroṣaparuṣaṃ yat kṛṣṇasarpānane dātuṃ gaṇḍacapeṭam ujjhitabhiyā hastaḥ samullāsitaḥ
children.translated_text: When a frog, croaking in angry harshness, raised its hand, casting off fear, to give a slap on the cheek into the mouth of a black snake,

children.text: yaccādhomukham akṣiṇī pidadhatā nāgena tatra sthitaṃ tat sarvaṃ viṣamantriṇo bhagavataḥ kasyāpi līlāyitam ||
children.translated_text: and when the snake stayed there, face turned downward and eyes closed, all that was the mere play of some blessed master of poison-charms.

children.text: mṛtyor āsyam ivātataṃ dhanur idaṃ cāśīviṣābhāḥ śarāḥ śikṣā sāpi jitārjunaprabhṛtikā sarvatra nimnā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: This bow is stretched out like the mouth of death; the arrows resemble venomous snakes; the training has conquered even <s>Arjuna</s> and the rest; everywhere the path leads downward.

children.text: antaḥ krauryam aho śaṭhasya madhuraṃ hā hāri geyaṃ mukhe vyādhasyāsya yathā bhaviṣyati tathā manye vanaṃ nirmṛgam ||
children.translated_text: Alas, within this rogue there is cruelty, while in his mouth is a sweet, charming song. I think that, just as this hunter intends, the forest will become devoid of animals.

children.text: ko 'yaṃ bhrāntiprakāras tava pavana padaṃ lokapādāhatīnāṃ tejasvivrātasevye nabhasi nayasi yat pāṃsupūraṃ pratiṣṭhām
children.translated_text: What sort of delusion is this, O wind, that you bring a mass of dust to a standing place in the sky, trodden by the feet of people and frequented by hosts of the brilliant?

children.text: yasminn utthāpyamāne jananayanapathopadravas tāvad āstāṃ kenopāyena sādhyo vapuṣi kaluṣatādoṣa eṣa tvayaiva ||
children.translated_text: When it is raised up, let the annoyance to people's line of sight be as it may; by what means can this fault of impurity in its body be cured by you yourself?

children.text: ete te vijigīṣavo nṛpagṛhadvārārpitāvekṣaṇāḥ kṣipyante vasuyācanāhitadhiyaḥ kopoddhatair vetribhiḥ
children.translated_text: These men, eager to conquer, fix their gaze on the doors of kings' houses; with minds intent on asking for wealth, they are thrown out by doorkeepers swollen with anger.

children.text: arthebhyo viṣayopabhogavirasair nākāri yair ādaras te tiṣṭhanti manasvinaḥ surasarittīre manohāriṇi ||
children.translated_text: Those high-spirited men who have shown no regard for wealth, being disgusted with the enjoyment of sense-objects, remain on the lovely bank of the heavenly river.

children.text: vātā vāntu kadambareṇuśabalā nṛtyantu sarpadviṣaḥ sotsāhā navatoyabhāraguravo muñcantu nādaṃ ghanāḥ
children.translated_text: Let the winds blow, variegated with kadamba pollen; let the enemies of serpents dance eagerly; let the clouds, heavy with the weight of fresh water, make their sound.

children.text: magnāṃ kāntaviyogaduḥkhadahane māṃ vīkṣya dīnānanāṃ vidyut kiṃ sphurasi tvam apy akaruṇe strītve 'pi tulye sati ||
children.translated_text: Seeing me, with a wretched face, sunk in the fire of grief at separation from my beloved, why do you too flash, O lightning, merciless one, though we share the same womanhood?

children.text: prāṇā yena samarpitās tava balād yenaivam utthāpitaḥ skandhe yena ciraṃ dhṛto 'si vidadhe yas te saparyām api
children.translated_text: He by whom your life was entrusted to you, by whose strength you were raised up in this way, by whom you were long carried on his shoulder, and who even performed service for you:

children.text: tasyāntaḥ smitamātrakeṇa janayañjīvāpahāraṃ kṣaṇād bhrātaḥ pratyupakāriṇāṃ dhuri paraṃ vetālalīlāyase ||
children.translated_text: by taking away that man's life in an instant with only a slight inner smile, brother, you play supremely the sport of a <s>vetāla</s> toward those who have helped you.

children.text: rajjvā diśaḥ pravitatāḥ salilaṃ viṣeṇa khātā mahī hutabhujā jvalitā vanāntāḥ
children.translated_text: The directions are stretched out with ropes; the water has been poisoned; the ground has been dug with pits; the forest interiors have been set blazing with fire;

children.text: vyādhāḥ padāny anusaranti gṛhītacāpāḥ kaṃ deśam āśrayatu yūthapatir mṛgāṇām ||
children.translated_text: hunters, bows in hand, follow the tracks. What region can the leader of the deer-herd take refuge in?

children.text: ayaṃ vārām eko nilaya iti ratnākara iti śrito 'smābhis tṛṣṇātaralitamanobhir jalanidhiḥ
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'This alone is the abode of waters; this is the jewel-mine,' we, our minds trembling with thirst, took refuge in the ocean.

children.text: ka evaṃ jānīte nijakarapuṭīkoṭaragataṃ kṣaṇād enaṃ tāmyattiminikaram āpāsyati muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who knows in this way whether the sage will, in a moment, drink up this mass of distressed sea-creatures contained in the hollow of his own joined hands?

children.text: viśālaṃ śālmalyā nayanasubhagaṃ vīkṣya kusumaṃ śukasyāsīd buddhiḥ phalam api bhaved asya sadṛśam
children.translated_text: Seeing the broad flower of the <s>śālmalī</s>, lovely to the eye, the parrot thought, "Its fruit too must be like this."

children.text: cirāsīnaṃ tasmiṃś ca phalam api daivāt pariṇataṃ vipāke tūlo 'ntaḥ sapadi marutā so 'py apahṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After sitting there a long time, by chance a fruit too ripened; but at maturity there was cotton inside, and that too was at once carried off by the wind.

children.text: sarvaprajāhitakṛte puruṣottamasya vāse samastavibudhaprathiteṣṭasiddhau
children.translated_text: In this ocean, the dwelling of <s>Puruṣottama</s>, made for the welfare of all creatures, famous among all the gods as the fulfillment of desired aims,

children.text: candrāṃśuvṛndavitatadyutim aty amuṣmin he kālakūṭa tava janma kathaṃ payodhau ||
children.translated_text: and filled with a radiance spread out by masses of moonbeams, O <s>Kālakūṭa</s>, how did your birth occur?

children.text: phalitaghanaviṭapavighaṭitapaṭudinakaramahasi lasati kalpatarau
children.translated_text: When the wish-fulfilling tree shines with dense fruit-bearing branches and with a brilliance that shatters the fierce sunlight,

children.text: chāyārthī kaḥ paśur api bhavati jaradvīrudhāṃ praṇayī ||
children.translated_text: what creature, even a beast, seeking shade, becomes attached to old creepers?
